# Keyboard navigation reaches homepage search and results refinement controls in order

> Prove the homepage search fields and CTA are reachable in order by Tab and the results-page Filters and Map controls are keyboard-accessible with visible focus indication.

## Step 1 @verifies ac-6, ac-8, ac-9

Open {{start_url}} on airbnb.co.in and, using keyboard navigation on the homepage search bar, move focus through the search controls until the Search button is reached, then assert the focus order is Where, Check-in, Check-out, Who, and Search.

## Step 2

Still using the web UI, complete a Homes search for Hanoi with Check-in {{check_in_date}}, Check-out {{check_out_date}}, and Who {{guest_count}}, and land on the Homes results page.

## Step 3 @verifies ac-29, ac-30, ac-31, ac-32

On the Homes results page, navigate by keyboard to the refinement controls, then assert the Filters and Map controls are keyboard-accessible and each shows a visible focus indicator when focused.

judgements.rationale: [self_critique] The check directly proves only the Filters control exposure from ac-27; the results-update assertion stayed narrower than 'all matching listings are shown' because gap-6 leaves the authoritative filter predicate unresolved, and gap g7 captures the missing reproducible filter/value pair.

[self_critique] The check directly proves map listing presence from ac-23. I kept the location-refinement assertion separate and avoided claiming a specific result-set predicate because gap-7 leaves the documented interaction unresolved, while gap g8 captures the missing concrete map target.

[self_critique] The assertions are limited to source-grounded keyboard focus order and visible focus indication, avoiding broader accessibility claims such as screen-reader behavior or all-tab-stop ordering outside the named controls. No negative keyboard case was added because the PRD states only positive accessibility requirements.
